title: Why did this number change: a question about a business number answered from approved definitions and tested queries, with the factor that moved it, where, and the query under the answer
request: Phase 8 (the owner's pattern 6): a metric_change kind with a semantic layer, the change decomposed into its factors in logs with a bootstrap over days, drilled down by dimension into mix against rate, a model that chooses tested templates and fills them, the query, source and dates under every answer, an action, and a replica with planted causes including a data gap.
plan: Write the replica first: two tables (door counts, tills by category), each planted cause on brands and stores of its own, the questions and what a careful analyst finds.
Write the library: the semantic layer contract, the templates as query plans, coverage, the decomposition and its intervals, the drill-down, the choice of template by name, model or rules.
Wire it: a library-only kind, the studio's SQLite runner, the campaign with a capped model arm, the gateway purpose and its data limit.
Measure on many seeds before any claim; review; fix; record.

decisions.decision: A why is decomposed in logs: the factors' log changes add up to the metric's exactly.
decisions.why: Shares of a product's change are only additive in logs; percentages of each factor do not add up.

decisions.decision: A factor moves only when its interval over days, one for all the factors searched (Bonferroni), excludes zero; segments likewise over every segment searched.
decisions.why: Three factors at 90% each named a move in about one steady question in four; with the family interval it was one in thirty.

decisions.decision: A gap is a day a ratio's denominator is missing or zero while its numerator is positive.
decisions.why: A closed day has no rows anywhere; a counter that failed while the tills sold breaks conversion, and summing the visitors there reads as a footfall fall.

decisions.decision: The core never reaches a database: each query is one plan, rendered as SQL with bound parameters and as its pandas computation; the host runs the SQL.
decisions.why: The core's boundary denies sqlite3 (17.1); a test runs both renderings and compares them, so the SQL shown is the computation made.

decisions.decision: The person's direction (down or up) is a parameter, read from the words or named.
decisions.why: A named template lost the question's 'down', and a move within the variation needs a direction to look for its segment.

decisions.decision: metric_change is a registry kind that runs only as a library; the router's catalogue covers the engine's kinds.
decisions.why: It has no outcome to train on; Home refuses to build it with its reason (FAMILY_NOT_RUN) rather than making a model of some column.

change: dclab_core.metric_change (SemanticLayer v1, MetricAnswer v1, Plan, Data, ask/answer/choose/rules/named, drill, coverage); dclab_core.replicas.mall_sales; dclab_core/prompts/metric_question.md; dclab_rnd.kinds.metric_change; dclab_rnd.metric_change (sqlite_runner, the campaign MCH-*); the gateway purpose metric_question; research/metric-root-cause; dclab-core 0.94.0; pattern 6 built.

findings.defect: A steady brand was said to have a factor that moved.
findings.scenario: Seeds 14 and 18 of 20: conversion +2.4% with its 90% interval above zero while sales moved within their variation.
findings.cause: Each of three factors had its own 90% interval: about one false move in four questions with nothing planted.
findings.fix: One interval for all the factors searched (Bonferroni) and for all the segments searched.

findings.defect: A planted cause's question was read by another cause.
findings.scenario: The failed counter's mall held the conversion brand's stores: its question would have been refused for a gap that was not its own.
findings.cause: Planted causes chose malls and brands independently.
findings.fix: Each cause on brands and stores of its own; the gap on one store; the steady brand kept out of the mall whose footfall fell.

findings.defect: A footfall question alone at the failed store read a false fall.
findings.scenario: metric_change on footfall at the store whose counter failed: -40%, answered.
findings.cause: Coverage checked only the ratios of the metric asked.
findings.fix: Every ratio whose denominator the answer reads is checked through its numerator.

findings.defect: The core imported sqlite3.
findings.scenario: test_core_contracts' boundary test refused dclab_core/metric_change.py.
findings.cause: The first version ran the SQL itself.
findings.fix: The plan's two renderings; the studio's SQLite runner in dclab_rnd.

findings.defect: The router's catalogue test asked every kind to be a route.
findings.scenario: test_solutions: metric_change is not in the catalogue.
findings.cause: The test iterated every kind though its name says the engine's kinds.
findings.fix: Scoped to the kinds the engine runs, with metric_change named as the one library kind.

findings.defect: A store's gap hid under the brand's other stores.
findings.scenario: 'Why is footfall down for Hollis?' was answered: footfall -10.7%, led by the mall whose counter had failed, with an action.
findings.cause: Coverage summed each table over the filters before looking for missing days.
findings.fix: Each ratio's two tables checked at the grain they share (the day and every dimension both hold), in every template.

findings.defect: A segment whose denominator was zero for a whole period crashed the drill-down.
findings.scenario: A store's footfall gone for a month: nan_to_num made an infinite rate finite, the contribution overflowed, the contract refused NaN.
findings.cause: No guard on a zero denominator inside the drill.
findings.fix: The drill gives no drill for a positive numerator over a zero denominator, or any number not finite; coverage refuses first.

findings.defect: A gap in the numerator's table was never a gap.
findings.scenario: Ten days of a store's tills deleted: conversion 'moved most', with an action about stock.
findings.cause: Only the denominator's missing days were checked.
findings.fix: A positive denominator with no numerator row is a gap too.

findings.defect: Periods outside the data were answered or crashed.
findings.scenario: A period running past the data's end answered -45%; October 2026 raised out of ask.
findings.cause: Only a period wholly outside was refused, the comparison never; the rules' errors were not caught.
findings.fix: The period and its comparison must lie in the data; an unanswerable choice is a refusal with what is missing.

findings.defect: Periods of unequal length were compared as totals.
findings.scenario: March against February: +19% for a brand with nothing planted, 10.7 points of it the three extra days.
findings.cause: Sums were compared as totals.
findings.fix: A sum is compared per calendar day, in the point and the bootstrap; the note says so.

findings.defect: A factor that moved could be dropped.
findings.scenario: Footfall within its variation ranked first, basket moved: the words said no factor moved.
findings.cause: Only the first ranked factor was tested.
findings.fix: The first factor that moved the way the metric did.

findings.defect: The planted segment could go unnamed.
findings.scenario: Seed 31: a mall up 3% within its variation led by size; the planted mall's fall was never tested.
findings.cause: The lead was the largest absolute contribution.
findings.fix: The lead is the segment that moved the factor most the way it moved.

findings.defect: Only the denominator's table held the dimension: wrong numbers.
findings.scenario: Visitors by door, tills without one: the contributions summed to 92.9 against a change of 27.9.
findings.cause: The first segment's denominator was read as the total.
findings.fix: No drill when the numerator's table lacks the dimension.

findings.defect: SQLite and pandas differed on empty values.
findings.scenario: A blanked category became the segment 'None' in SQL, dropped in pandas.
findings.cause: SQL grouped NULL as a value.
findings.fix: A key column's empty value is never a segment, in both renderings.

findings.defect: The words were misread.
findings.scenario: A month without a year read September; 'last month' read July when the data ended on the 1st; a side remark about prices refused the question.
findings.cause: No rule for a month alone; the last whole month was computed from MonthBegin; any not-held word refused.
findings.fix: The latest whole occurrence of a month, said; the last whole month from the first of the last month; a not-held concept refuses only when asked about as a cause or when no metric is named, else it is said beside the answer.

findings.defect: The named path dropped unknown keys.
findings.scenario: 'brnad=Fenn' answered for the whole group.
findings.cause: Keys that were not dimensions were ignored.
findings.fix: An unknown key is refused.

findings.defect: The menu could exceed the purpose's limit or crash.
findings.scenario: Four dimensions of fifty values sent 200 against the limit of 150; thirteen raised EvidenceError out of ask.
findings.cause: Fifty values per dimension, no total; the evidence error was not caught.
findings.fix: At most 150 values in all, shared; an evidence error leaves the rules' reading.

findings.defect: Contract limits crashed valid input.
findings.scenario: A 2001-character question, or many metrics in a refusal's reason, raised a ValidationError.
findings.cause: Tight maxima on text that is kept whole.
findings.fix: The question kept whole (100,000), reasons list at most twelve names.

findings.defect: A store that does not exist answered 0.
findings.scenario: Arlo's sales in a mall it has no store in: 'Sales: 0'.
findings.cause: An empty result summed to zero.
findings.fix: No rows is no number: refused.

findings.defect: The model's raw reply was lost.
findings.scenario: Only the validated choice or an error string was kept.
findings.cause: Capture after validation only.
findings.fix: The reply is kept whole before it is checked.

findings.defect: Detection took over other problems.
findings.scenario: 'Forecast next week's sales; why are sales down in winter?' became metric_change; a churn question with a why became metric_change.
findings.cause: Its specificity ranked it above the engine's kinds.
findings.fix: It steps aside when another specific kind's words match or the sentence reads as a task.

findings.defect: The gate's generated files were behind.
findings.scenario: No kinds_v1 record, the harness gate stale, the capability matrix not rebuilt, conclusions written before records.
findings.cause: The close-out had not run.
findings.fix: KND-022, the rebuilds, agent-eval and harness-eval, conclusions from the MCH records.

findings.defect: The first live arm ran with no model.
findings.scenario: MCH-002's first attempt: no requests, no spend, and the record said 'model'.
findings.cause: The CLI did not load the provider's .env, and nothing refused an arm no model answered.
findings.fix: The CLI loads .env, uses the workspace's gateway, refuses to run when nothing serves the purpose and to write an arm that asked nothing; the empty record was never kept.

findings.defect: Right refusals were judged wrong.
findings.scenario: MCH-002: the competitor and margin paraphrases refused correctly, naming what the data would need.
findings.cause: The prompt asked for what the data would need; the judge reads the concept's name.
findings.fix: The prompt asks for the concept's name, and a refusal naming its needs is read as the concept.

findings.defect: Factors and segments each spent a 10% error budget.
findings.scenario: After the review's fixes the steady brand named a move in 4 of 30 seeds.
findings.cause: Two families, each at 10%.
findings.fix: One 10% budget, half to the factors and half to the segments.

measurements.name: the rules on the mall sales replica's planted questions, sixty seeds
measurements.gate: every planted cause found and ranked first; refusals with what is missing
measurements.result: 477 of 480: 60 of 60 for the footfall drop, the conversion drop, the mix, the data gap, the competitor and the margin; 59 of 60 for the footfall's mall; 58 of 60 for the steady brand
measurements.against_gate: met on every planted cause but the designed false-move rate
limits: The steady brand may name a move at the family's error rate.

measurements.name: the kind's acceptance (KND-022) and the rules campaign (MCH-001)
measurements.gate: the kind's decisions on three seeds
measurements.result: 27 of 27 checks on three seeds; the rules reach 8 of 8 questions in their words and 6 of 6 named, and 2 of 8 paraphrases
limits: The rules read only the words they were written for.

measurements.name: the product's model choosing the template on the paraphrases (MCH-003, live)
measurements.gate: the model's choice is validated and its answer judged as the rules' is
measurements.result: 24 of 24 paraphrases on three seeds against the rules' 6 of 24, 24 requests, no failure, EUR 0.0999
measurements.against_gate: the model reads the other words; nothing is served until it is switched on
limits: The paraphrases were written by the same author as the questions.

outcome: DCLab answers why a business number moved from approved definitions and tested queries: the factor, where, by how much, with the SQL that made the numbers, or a refusal that says what is missing; a model reads other words into a tested template.
lessons: Planted causes must not share their units: a cause one question did not ask about can still change its answer.
Several intervals at 90% each are a much weaker claim than one: say how many were searched.
A gap must be checked at the grain where it happens: a total hides a store.
A live arm that asks nothing must refuse to be written: a fallback reads as a measurement.
A judge and a prompt must ask for the same thing before a model's miss is called a miss.
Build generated files with another package's untracked files held aside: the knowledge base committed with 30.17 already held 30.20's track.
risks: The paraphrases are one author's; an independent writer's set is the next measurement.
The kind runs as a library: no project, no Home path beyond the refusal.
Coverage reads only the ratios of the layer; a gap in a sum no ratio divides is unseen.
